arxiv-2102-09679.title: Improved Multi-Pass Streaming Algorithms for Submodular Maximization with Matroid Constraints Thanks: A preliminary version of this work was presented at the International Conference on Approximation Algorithms for Combinatorial Optimization Problems (APPROX 2020). This work was funded by the grants
arxiv-2102-09679.creator: Chien-Chung Huang, Theophile ThieryJustin Ward
arxiv-2102-09679.description: Abstract We give improved multi-pass streaming algorithms for the problem of maximizing a monotone or arbitrary non-negative submodular function subject to a general p p -matchoid constraint in the model in which elements of the ground set arrive one at a time in a stream.

arxiv-2102-12662.title: A sandwich in thin Lie algebras
arxiv-2102-12662.creator: Sandro Mattarei
arxiv-2102-12662.description: Abstract . A thin Lie algebra is a Lie algebra L L , graded over the positive integers, with its first homogeneous component L 1 L_{1} of dimension two and generating L L , and such that each nonzero ideal of L L lies between consecutive terms of its lower central series.

arxiv-2106-15964.title: AI-Based Secure NOMA and Cognitive Radio enabled Green Communications: Channel State Information and Battery Value Uncertainties
arxiv-2106-15964.creator: Saeed Sheikhzadeh, Mohsen Pourghasemian, Mohammad R. Javan, Nader Mokari, Eduard A. Jorswieck
arxiv-2106-15964.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Saeed Sheikhzadeh, Mohsen Pourghasemian, Mohammad R. Javan, Nader Mokari, Eduard A. Jorswieck. In this paper, the security-aware robust resource allocation in energy harvesting cognitive radio networks is considered with cooperation between two transmitters while there are uncertainties in channel gains and battery energy value. To be specific, the primary access point harvests energy from the green resource and uses time switching protocol to send the energy and data towards the secondary access point (SAP).

arxiv-2108-03972.title: An inhibited laser
arxiv-2108-03972.creator: Tiantian Shi 1 , Duo Pan 1 & Jingbiao Chen 1,∗
arxiv-2108-03972.description: Abstract Traditional lasers function using resonant cavities, in which the round-trip optical path is exactly equal to an integer multiple of the intracavity wavelengths to constructively enhance the spontaneous emission rate. By taking advantage of the enhancement from the resonant cavity, the narrowest sub-10-mHz-linewidth laser and a 10 -16 -fractional-frequency-stability superradiant active optical clock (AOC) have been achieved.

arxiv-2112-06826.title: BScNets: Block Simplicial Complex Neural Networks
arxiv-2112-06826.creator: Yuzhou Chen, Yulia R. Gel, H. Vincent Poor
arxiv-2112-06826.description: Abstract Simplicial neural networks (SNN) have recently emerged as the newest direction in graph learning which expands the idea of convolutional architectures from node space to simplicial complexes on graphs. Instead of pre-dominantly assessing pairwise relations among nodes as in the current practice, simplicial complexes allow us to describe higher-order interactions and multi-node graph structures.

arxiv-2204-05872.title: Robust Quantification of Gender Disparity in Pre-Modern English Literature using Natural Language Processing
arxiv-2204-05872.creator: Akarsh Nagaraj, Mayank Kejriwal
arxiv-2204-05872.description: Abstract . Research has continued to shed light on the extent and significance of gender disparity in social, cultural and economic spheres. More recently, computational tools from the Natural Language Processing (NLP) literature have been proposed for measuring such disparity using relatively extensive datasets and empirically rigorous methodologies.

arxiv-2207-04937.title: Spin-Orbit Proximity Effect in Bi/Co Multilayer: The Role of Interface Scattering
arxiv-2207-04937.creator: Arthur Casa Nova Nonnig, Alexandre da Cas Viegas, Fabiano Mesquita da Rosa, Paulo Pureur, Milton Andre Tumelero
arxiv-2207-04937.description: Abstract The Spin-Orbit Proximity Effect is the raise of Spin-Orbit Coupling at a layer near to the interface with a strong spin-orbit material. It has been seen in several system such as graphene and ferromagnetic layers. The control of the Spin-Orbit Coupling can be a pathway to discover novel and exotic phases in superconductor and semimetallic systems.

arxiv-2210-05259.title: Polarized primordial gravitational waves in spatial covariant gravities
arxiv-2210-05259.creator: Tao Zhu a,b, Wen Zhao c,d, Anzhong Wang e
arxiv-2210-05259.description: Abstract The spatial covariant gravities provide a natural way to including odd-order spatial derivative terms into the gravitational action, which breaks the parity symmetry at gravitational sector. A lot of parity-violating scalar-tensor theories can be mapped to the spatial covariant framework by imposing the unitary gauge.

arxiv-2211-13653.title: Scalar field dark matter and dark energy: A hybrid model for the dark sector
arxiv-2211-13653.creator: Carsten van de Bruck, Gaspard Poulot, Elsa M. Teixeira
arxiv-2211-13653.description: Abstract Diverse cosmological and astrophysical observations strongly hint at the presence of dark matter and dark energy in the Universe. One of the main goals of Cosmology is to explain the nature of these two components. It may well be that both dark matter and dark energy have a common origin.

arxiv-2310-06822.title: Neural Bounding 593 Conference: Special Interest Group on Computer Graphics and Interactive Techniques Conference Conference Papers ’24; July 27-August 1, 2024; Denver, CO, USA Special Interest Group on Computer Graphics and Interactive Techniques Conference Conference Papers ’24 (SIGGRAPH Conferenc
arxiv-2310-06822.creator: Stephanie Wenxin Liu, Michael Fischer, Paul D. Yoo, Tobias Ritschel
arxiv-2310-06822.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Stephanie Wenxin Liu, Michael Fischer, Paul D. Yoo, Tobias Ritschel. Bounding volumes are an established concept in computer graphics and vision tasks but have seen little change since their early inception. In this work, we study the use of neural networks as bounding volumes. Our key observation is that bounding, which so far has primarily been considered a problem of computational geometry, can be redefined as a problem of learning to classify space into free or occupied.

arxiv-2312-03962.title: Lyapunov exponents and shear-induced chaos for a Hopf bifurcation with additive noise
arxiv-2312-03962.creator: Peter H. Baxendale
arxiv-2312-03962.description: Abstract This paper considers the effect of additive white noise on the normal form for the supercritical Hopf bifurcation in 2 dimensions. The main results involve the asymptotic behavior of the top Lyapunov exponent λ \lambda associated with this random dynamical system as one or more of the parameters in the system tend to 0 or ∞ \infty .

arxiv-2412-11896.title: Classification of Spontaneous and Scripted Speech for Multilingual Audio
arxiv-2412-11896.creator: Shahar Elisha, Andrew McDowell, Mariano Beguerisse-Díaz, Emmanouil Benetos
arxiv-2412-11896.description: Abstract Distinguishing scripted from spontaneous speech is an essential tool for better understanding how speech styles influence speech processing research. It can also improve recommendation systems and discovery experiences for media users through better segmentation of large recorded speech catalogues. This paper addresses the challenge of building a classifier that generalises well across different formats and languages.

arxiv-2503-17996.title: Identifying Ising and percolation phase transitions based on KAN method
arxiv-2503-17996.creator: Dian Xu, Shanshan Wang, Wei Li, Weibing Deng, Feng Gao, Jianmin Shen
arxiv-2503-17996.description: Abstract Modern machine learning, grounded in the Universal Approximation Theorem, has achieved significant success in the study of phase transitions in both equilibrium and non-equilibrium systems. However, identifying the critical points of percolation models using raw configurations remains a challenging and intriguing problem.

A topological superconductor, characterized by either a chiral order parameter [ 1 , 2 ] or a chiral topological surface state in proximity to bulk superconductivity [ 3 ] , is foundational to topological quantum computing.

arxiv-2511-04658.title: Where to Experiment? Site Selection Under Distribution Shift via Optimal Transport and Wasserstein DRO
arxiv-2511-04658.creator: Adam Bouyamourn
arxiv-2511-04658.description: Abstract How should researchers select experimental sites when the deployment population may differ from observed data? I formulate the problem of experimental site selection as an optimal transport problem , developing methods to minimize downstream estimation error by choosing sites that minimize the Wasserstein distance between population and sample covariate distributions.

arxiv-2601-13548.title: Patterning: The Dual of Interpretability
arxiv-2601-13548.creator: George Wang, Daniel Murfet
arxiv-2601-13548.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by George Wang, Daniel Murfet. Mechanistic interpretability aims to understand how neural networks generalize beyond their training data by reverse-engineering their internal structures. We introduce patterning as the dual problem: given a desired form of generalization, determine what training data produces it. Our approach is based on susceptibilities , which measure how posterior expectation values of observables respond to infinitesimal shifts in the data distribution. Inverting this linear response relationship yields the data intervention that steers the model toward a target internal configuration.

pmc-10567561.creator: Xiangling Meng, David Yao, Kent Imaizumi, Xiaoyu Chen, Kevin W. Kelley, Noah Reis, Mayuri Vijay Thete, Arpana Arjun McKinney, Shravanti Kulkarni, Georgia Panagiotakos, Michael C. Bassik, Sergiu P. Pașca
pmc-10567561.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). The assembly of cortical circuits involves the generation and migration of interneurons from the ventral to the dorsal forebrain1–3, which has been challenging to study at inaccessible stages of late gestation and early postnatal human development4. Autism spectrum disorder and other neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) have been associated with abnormal cortical interneuron development5, but which of these NDD genes affect interneuron generation and migration, and how they mediate these effects remains unknown.

pmc-11432244.title: The Effect of Blood Flow Restriction during Low-Load Resistance Training Unit on Knee Flexor Muscle Fatigue in Recreational Athletes: A Randomized Double-Blinded Placebo-Controlled Pilot Study
pmc-11432244.creator: Aleksandra Królikowska, Maciej Daszkiewicz, Julia Kocel, George Mihai Avram, Łukasz Oleksy, Robert Prill, Jarosław Witkowski, Krzysztof Korolczuk, Anna Kołcz, Paweł Reichert, Nicholas David Clement
pmc-11432244.description: Background/Objectives: Despite the growing popularity of training with a controlled form of vascular occlusion, known as blood flow restriction (BFR) training, in the rehabilitation of orthopedic patients and sports medicine, there remains ample space for understanding the basis of its mechanism.

pmc-11494204.title: Time-dependent neural arbitration between cue associative and episodic fear memories
pmc-11494204.creator: Aurelio Cortese, Ryu Ohata, Maria Alemany-González, Norimichi Kitagawa, Hiroshi Imamizu, Ai Koizumi
pmc-11494204.description: After traumatic events, simple cue-threat associative memories strengthen while episodic memories become incoherent. However, how the brain prioritises cue associations over episodic coding of traumatic events remains unclear. Here, we developed an original episodic threat conditioning paradigm in which participants concurrently form two memory representations: cue associations and episodic cue sequence.

pmc-11519312.title: Acceptability of Four Intervention Components Supporting Medication Adherence in Women with Breast Cancer: a Process Evaluation of a Fractional Factorial Pilot Optimization Trial
pmc-11519312.creator: Sophie M C Green, Nikki Rousseau, Louise H Hall, David P French, Christopher D Graham, Kelly E Lloyd, Michelle Collinson, Pei Loo Ow, Christopher Taylor, Daniel Howdon, Robbie Foy, Rebecca Walwyn, Jane Clark, Catherine Parbutt, Jo Waller, Jacqueline Buxton, Sally J L Moore, Galina Velikova, Amanda F
pmc-11519312.description: Adjuvant endocrine therapy (AET) reduces mortality in early-stage breast cancer, but adherence is low. We developed a multicomponent intervention to support AET adherence comprising: text messages, information leaflet, acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT), and side-effect website. Guided by the multiphase optimization strategy, the intervention components were tested in the ROSETA pilot optimization trial. Our mixed-methods process evaluation investigated component acceptability.

pmc-11638622.title: Decellularized adipose matrix hydrogel-based in situ delivery of antagomiR-150-5p for rat abdominal aortic aneurysm therapy
pmc-11638622.creator: Xin Chen, Shoushuai Wang, Weijian Hou, Yanhui Zhang, Yapeng Hou, Hao Tong, Xiaoxin Zhang, Yue Liu, Ruoxuan Yang, Xiang Li, Qin Fang, Jun Fan
pmc-11638622.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a progressive aortic disease featured by inflammation, vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) depletion, and elastin degradation. MicroRNAs were related to AAA formation, which bring the approach for precise and targeted drug therapy for AAA. We developed a new strategy based on decellularized adipose matrix (DAM) hydrogel immobilized on the adventitia to release antagomiR-150-5p for preventing the AAA development. In this study, Cacl2-induced and elastase-induced rat AAA models were established.

pmc-11691722.title: HARMONIZATION OF LATER-LIFE COGNITIVE FUNCTION ACROSS POPULATION-BASED COHORT STUDIES: RESULTS FROM HRS AND NHATS
pmc-11691722.creator: Diefei Chen, Vishaldeep Sekhon, David Roth, Christopher Kaufmann, Alden Gross
pmc-11691722.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Population-based cohort studies offer unique opportunities to study characteristics of people at greatest risk for cognitive decline. Harmonizing large, well-characterized cohorts powers investigations into subgroups or rare exposures/outcomes in their associations with cognitive decline. We derived a harmonized cognition score based on cognitive tests from the Health and Retirement Study (HRS) and the National Health and Aging Trends Study (NHATS), two of the largest nationally representative cohorts of older adults in the US.

pmc-12508151.title: Electrical control of topological 3Q state in intercalated van der Waals antiferromagnet Cox-TaS2
pmc-12508151.creator: Junghyun Kim, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Pyeongjae Park, Woonghee Cho, Hyuncheol Kim, Han-Jin Noh, Je-Geun Park
pmc-12508151.description: Van der Waals (vdW) magnets have opened a new avenue of opportunities encompassing various interesting phases. Co1/3TaS2–an intercalated metallic vdW antiferromagnet–is one of the latest additions to this growing list of materials due to its unique topologically nontrivial triple-Q (3Q) ground state.

pmc-12533470.title: The correlation between smoking and preoperative deep venous thrombosis after hip fracture in geriatric patients: a propensity score-matched study
pmc-12533470.creator: Wanyun Tang, Runzhuo Li
pmc-12533470.description: PurposeThis study aimed to investigate the association between smoking and the incidence of preoperative deep venous thrombosis (DVT) after hip fracture in geriatric patients.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study included 1,190 geriatric patients who underwent surgery for hip fractures. Patients were categorized into smokers and non-smokers based on their smoking history.

pmc-13167470.title: MicroSplit: semantic unmixing of fluorescent microscopy data
pmc-13167470.creator: Ashesh Ashesh, Federico Carrara, Igor Zubarev, Vera Galinova, Melisande Croft, Melissa Pezzotti, Daozheng Gong, Francesca Casagrande, Elisa Colombo, Stefania Giussani, Elena Restelli, Eugenia Cammarota, Juan Manuel Battagliotti, Nikolai Klena, Moises Di Sante, Raghabendra Adhikari, Daniel Feliciano,
pmc-13167470.description: Fluorescence microscopy is constrained by optical limits, fluorophore chemistry and finite photon budgets, imposing trade-offs between imaging speed, resolution and phototoxicity. Here we introduce MicroSplit, a deep learning-based computational multiplexing method that enables multiple cellular structures to be imaged simultaneously in a single fluorescent channel and then computationally unmixed.

pmc-13508165.title: Toward a neuroergonomic understanding of spatial disorientation
pmc-13508165.creator: Jerome Carriot, Isabelle Mackrous, Pascale Brochu, Simon Corcos, Marc-Antoine Pelletier, Maurice J. Chacron
pmc-13508165.description: Despite decades of research, spatial disorientation, which is the incorrect perception of one’s orientation relative to gravity, remains one of the leading causes of aviation mishaps. In this mini-review, we highlight the role of the vestibular system towards generating disorientation.

pmc-13562499.title: Prediction of physicochemical properties of organic compounds using degree-based topological indices and machine learning models

pmc-13670181.creator: Petra E M Tasseron‐Dries, Hanneke J A Smaling, Wilco P Achterberg, Miharu Nakanishi, Jenny T van der Steen
pmc-13670181.description: ObjectivesChallenging behavior and pain are common in nursing home residents with dementia. STA OP! with family is a multidisciplinary stepwise method that involves family in addressing challenging behavior and pain. This study examines the impact of STA OP! with family on residents, family, and nursing staff.
